content_of_post_to_comment:
Context: I’m very high functioning for someone who has adhd and who’s not medicated, primarily because where I come from people don’t entertain most mental conditions, let alone diagnose them, so I got diagnosed much later in life and by then I had picked up every trick in the book that could help me focus and bring stability in my life, below are a few i consider to be the best.

I plan tomorrow today: I write down my top 3 tasks the night before so I don't waste morning brainpower deciding what to do. In addition to the three tasks I’ll also write down things I need to do daily like gym, consuming 120gs protein etc

I timeblock as much as I can: I schedule my day into specific time chunks instead of looking at one massive, overwhelming list. In the planner where I write the tasks for the next day, there’s also a schedule listed with hours of the day, i will plug in the tasks in specific hours and i’ll also plug in the rest of the daily activities (i.e 7 pm - gym 9pm - dinner 10:30 pm - vitamins, water floss, brush teeth 11 pm - in bed )

I make social media less addictive: I access all my social media platforms through an app that lets me hide feeds, reels etc, which prevents me from doomscrolling but still lets me communicate with friends. I also have it so that at exactly 10 pm all my feeds automatically hide and stay locked till 8 am

I wake up and sleep at the exact same time: This one is a weird one, mainly because its hard, so I wake up at 7 am and sleep at 11 pm every night, but the main facilitator for this is looking at the sun for like 10 to 20 seconds when I wake up, this helps program your circadian rhythm but during the winter months this becomes harder and my sleep schedule begins to mess up. But when I do have it down, I'm the most productive and least stressed

I wear a wristwatch: This was a game changer, having a wrist watch makes you a lot more aware of the time passing and prevents you from losing hours in a distraction.

I journal every morning: Doing a quick brain dump first thing clears out all the mental noise before I start my day. I don’t know about you guys but my mind likes to wander and it likes to wander deeply, and often ill get these eureka moments that i cant stop obsessing over or thinking about and it prevents me from getting other stuff done, so every morning I dump all these ideas into a journal, it also takes the pressure off of me to remember them, knowing that i’ve “uploaded” them lets my brain move on to other things
